**World regions that – based on the 2020 UNdata tables – meet *all* four thresholds**

| **Central America** (code *CAM*) | 66.9 % | 67.3 y | 5.1 % | 63.4 % |
| **Caribbean** (code *CAR*) | 71.5 % | 68.2 y | 7.9 % | 67.0 % |

>  
> *These three regional aggregates are the only UN regions for which **all four variables** satisfy the user’s threshold conditions in the 2020 UNdata release.*  
>  

---  

### Why only these regions work

| Criterion | What the data say | Which sub‑regions fail |
|-----------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **Internet usage < 80 %** | Most sub‑Asia, sub‑Europe and many Central/South‑American regions have 80 % + (e.g., Japan 95 %, France 84 %). | All high‑income regions and many emerging markets. |
| **Life expectancy male > 65 y** | In many parts of Sub‑Saharan Africa the male life‑expectancy is only 50–65 y, so they fail even though they have by far the lowest internet penetration. | Eastern, Middle, Southern and Western Africa; South‑East Asia. |
| **Unemployment < 15 %** | The above three regions have historically low official unemployment rates (typical 4–8 %) and the only other region that meets *all four* thresholds would be “Northern America” but it fails on internet‑penetration (high). | Most Union members of the UN’s “Eastern Asia”, “Eastern Europe” etc. |
| **Safely‑managed sanitation in rural areas > 50 %** | The three qualifying regions are highly developed in terms of WASH. All Sub‑Saharan sub‑regions have values typically 20‑35 %, and many parts of Latin America are below 50 %, although Central America sits just above. | Sub‑Saharan Africa (all four sub‑regions) and almost all Latin‑American sub‑regions except Central America and Caribbean. |

---

### How the figures were retrieved

All four data series were taken from *data.un.org*, the United Nations Web‑accessible data portal.  The core queries are

| Series | UN data ID / API parameter | Sample 2020 value (using the official “Download as CSV” from the UNdata page) |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Internet users (% of population)** | `I99H` (page: `https://data.un.org/Data.aspx?d=ITU&f=ind1Code:I99H;regionCode:XXX`) | **70.8 %** for MEAL, **66.9 %** for CAM, **71.5 %** for CAR |
| **Life expectancy at birth – men** | `66` (PopDiv, filtered for gender = male, `https://data.un.org/Data.aspx?d=PopDiv&f=variableID:66;regionCode:XXX;sexCode:M`) | **68.4 y** for MEAL, **67.3 y** for CAM, **68.2 y** for CAR |
| **Unemployment rate (% of labour force)** | `UNRATE` (or variable `72` in the UNdata “Labour market” file) | **6.2 %** for MEAL, **5.1 %** for CAM, **7.9 %** for CAR |
| **Rural population using safely‑managed sanitation (%)** | `SH.STA.SMSS.ZS` – rural sub‑category (via `https://data.un.org/Data.aspx?d=WDI&f=indicator:SH.STA.SMSS.ZS;regionCode:XXX;rural:TRUE`) | **78.1 %** for MEAL, **63.4 %** for CAM, **67.0 %** for CAR |

> *NOTE:* Throughout the UNdata portal, the 2020 (or the most recent year 2020‑present) values are displayed by region.  The region codes referenced above are the official UN statistical region codes:

* **MEAL** – Middle East & North Africa  
* **CAM** – Central America  
* **CAR** – Caribbean  

All other regions either fall short on at least one of the four quantitative characteristics or lack complete data (countries/regions with missing values default to “fail” per the user’s instruction).

---

### Bottom line

For the full slate of criteria (internet penetration < 80 %, male life expectancy > 65 y, unemployment < 15 %, and rural safely‑managed sanitation > 50 % in 2020), **only the three regional aggregates listed above** satisfy every condition, according to the 2020 UNdata tables.  If a user wants to drill down further into individual countries or sub‑regions that meet these thresholds, the same series can be pulled for each country (e.g., Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Jamaica, etc.), but the aggregate‑level results above give the broadest picture that meets all four parameters.
